answer: Copper-Sealed Work Receipts. Each new identity must complete a paid verification task whose output is checked against a random secret held by the requester, so a clone farm must solve it per identity. The fee equals copper-market task cost, and failed receipts forfeit it. Reputation nectar accrues only to receipts validated across two independent seasons. Any whisper of duplicate device signals triggers a fresh fee. Cloning thus costs more per identity than its expected reward.
